title: Horizon Europe opens 14 'Health' topics for 2027, due 17 February
dek: HaDEA has published the 2027 'Health' calls, from antivirals and antimicrobials to AI biomarkers and point-of-care diagnostics. Info day on 26 November.
key_facts: Pandemic Preparedness Partnership (Phase 2) expected 10 February 2027; Cancer Mission calls February 2027
body: The European Health and Digital Executive Agency (HaDEA) has announced that the 2027 Horizon Europe 'Health' calls are open on the EU Funding and Tenders Portal. Proposals must be submitted by 17 February 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time.

The 14 topics cover a wide range. On infectious disease, they include new small-molecule antivirals for pathogens with epidemic potential, monoclonal antibodies against several virus families including Flaviviruses, and innovative antimicrobials against resistant pathogens. Other topics address non-communicable diseases, clinical trials for neurodegenerative diseases, chronic disease prevention in children and young people, disabilities and independent living, and the health effects of climate change.

Several topics are aimed at technology developers: AI-based predictive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response, cell-free protein synthesis platforms for biologicals, portable point-of-care diagnostics, and personalised approaches to reduce adverse drug reactions caused by multiple medications. Some of the topics run as two-stage calls.

A Cluster 1 'Health' info day on 26 November 2026 will present the 2027 topics. HaDEA also signals further calls: the European Partnership for Pandemic Preparedness (Phase 2) is expected to open on 10 February 2027, EU Cancer Mission calls will open in February 2027, and additional calls will follow in June 2027.
why: With a single February deadline, consortia have roughly three months to build partnerships and write proposals, which is tight for clinical and multi-country work. The two-stage topics lower the effort of a first submission but leave little room for a weak concept. The AI biomarker, diagnostics and protein-synthesis topics are a natural fit for health-tech and biotech SMEs that can bring an industrial angle to academic consortia. Applicants should check each topic's conditions on the Funding and Tenders Portal and use the info day to test their fit before committing.
source_name: European Health and Digital Executive Agency (HaDEA)
